title: Staying in Paris in 1948; Nicole Barclay picks him for the Paris Festival
summary: He stayed on after the tour, returned to New York for the winter, and in spring Nicole Barclay insisted he lead the group for the first Paris Festival with Miles, Tadd, Moody, Bird and Max.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: After the band finished working, I stayed on, you know.
And John, he went to study with a pianist, Madame Proto, to study piano. So he stayed over with me, you know.

So I stayed, from where we finished our work in February, and the band went back, so Dizzy said, 'You're not coming?' I said, 'No, I'm not going back. I'm not going back to hell again, you know, with all those agents down my throat.' So I stayed over and Dizzy took my drums back. And John and I, we left in August, in August of '48. So I stayed all winter in New York.
No, in New York. I left Paris in August.
I stayed in New York all winter, and that

spring, Madame Nicole Barclay, who owned the Barclay Record Company here, she came to New York to form a group to play the First Paris Festival. So she said right away, "I want Kenny Clarke first." Now, you'll get whoever else you want, but Kenny Clarke is first." Now, this was what she told the agents, so they were up in the air. They didn't know what to do. So she said, "Now, I want him, first. Otherwise, you forget it. I'll get him to pick the musicians." Which would have meant it would have cut off their percentage. So they shopped around and got Miles, Tadd, they got all the people that I liked, you know. They were trying to make me happy, because they knew that I was going to lead this whole thing. I had spurned the whole thing. So they got Moody, Tadd, Miles, Barney Spielman bass, and myself. Five pieces. And they got Bird, Max, Al Haig, all my friends. You see how it works out? Because if they had chosen someone against my wishes, then I would have said, "No, Nicole, we don't take him." So they tried to find every one who they thought I would approve of.
And there was Bird, Max, Al Haig, Tommy Potter.
Oh, Max. Well, you were going to be playing drums, weren't you?
It was the First Paris Festival.
So we were picking out the musicians to make this festival.
